Rule that keeps this file true: any commit that edits a copied artifact must update that artifact's repo_sha256 in the same commit, and any commit that moves one must update its repo_path too. **2026-09-20, card t_0cc793fb:** the `kitprobes` stage and `tools/kit-probes/tidy-baseline.sh` were taken from the kit at the revision above — a fix that must propagate ships a probe, and this copy now runs it in its own gate. `revision` moved to that commit because these entries come from it; the earlier entries are still the fb387f2 wiring, and the kit files behind them have not changed between the two commits (the ones that did — `templates/cpp/ci.sh`, `templates/hooks/pre-push` — were ported in this same commit). **2026-09-20, later the same day (still card t_0cc793fb):** `revision` moved to 951608c2675a… for two more artifacts from the kit — the gate's dispatch guards (a stage that dies or returns non-zero without a verdict can no longer leave a green run; measured on this gate's own `local -a sources`, see INCIDENTS.md) and that fix's own probe `tools/kit-probes/gate-stage-guards.sh`. Between the previous revision and this one the kit changed only `templates/cpp/ci.sh`, `INCIDENTS.md`, `DESIGN-NOTES.md` and the new probe; the entries behind the other files are unchanged by it. **2026-09-20, card t_45a28893:** `tools/ci.sh` gained an ELEVENTH stage the kit does not have, `release` — no stage here configured an optimized build while the Pages workflow builds -O3 -DNDEBUG (JSOM's subproject defaults CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE to Release), which is how a red deploy and a broken `./build.sh` stayed invisible behind a green local gate. With it: `CI_RELEASE_BUILD_DIR`/`CI_RELEASE_BUILD_TYPE` in tools/ci.sh and .ci.env.example, `release` in the pre-push list, an `Optimized builds` line in CODING_STANDARDS.md, and the optimized-build entry in INCIDENTS.md now names the stage as its check. `revision` above is UNCHANGED: nothing in this change came from the kit, so it is a repo-local addition, not a port. **2026-09-20, card t_4a81d75f:** `tools/ci.sh` gained a TWELFTH stage the kit does not have, `docs` — this repo's own documentation pipeline (66 executed examples, operator coverage, the generated reference and the two published indexes) had only ever run in .github/workflows/docs.yml, so nothing local saw 14 documented examples disagree with the engine or the reference the Pages site publishes go stale for seven months (INCIDENTS.md, same day). With it: `docs` in CI_DEFAULT_STAGES and in the pre-push list, python3 + PyYAML as gate prerequisites that FAIL rather than SKIP, and a paragraph for it in .ci.env.example's overrides section. `revision` above is UNCHANGED: nothing here came from the kit. **2026-09-20, card t_ce87d13e:** prose only, in four artifacts — the `release` stage's rationale no longer cites JSOM's subproject defaulting `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` to Release. That mechanism is gone: JSOM's cache writes are gated on `JSOM_IS_TOP_LEVEL` (card `t_772eabd9`), so the Pages workflow's build type is empty and it configures at CMake's -O0 — measured 2026-09-20 on a fresh configure of this repo with no build type passed: `Build type:` blank in the configure output, and no `-O` flag in the compile lines the generated database holds. The stage's live reason is the optimized configurations that exist here: `./build.sh` (Release) and an optimized consumer (jsonTools passes `CI_BUILD_TYPE=Release`). The dated notes above are left as the record of what those commits did and are NOT re-dated; what changed is the passages in tools/ci.sh, .ci.env.example, .githooks/pre-push and INCIDENTS.md that stated the dead mechanism in the present tense. Only those four `repo_sha256` values moved: nothing here came from the kit, so `revision` and every `kit_sha256` are unchanged (the kit's HEAD has since advanced past the recorded revision — whether to move it is a separate sync question, not this card's). **2026-09-20, card t_fb62d8fa:** the record gained the kit's per-fix lists (docs/KIT-REVISION-CONVENTION.md, 'Exact file shape'), so what this copy has and has not taken from the kit is machine-readable instead of prose. `adopted_fixes` names the two probes this copy carries, with the kit revision each fix came from -- and that claim is now CHECKED, not just asserted: the record checker runs each probe against tools/ci.sh, and a claim whose probe is absent or fails is a record failure. `declined_fixes` records the kit's `optimized-build-stage` as an ARTIFACT declined, NOT a behaviour missing: this repo built its own second configuration first -- the `release` stage in tools/ci.sh (card t_45a28893), which the kit then generalised into templates/cpp/ci.sh -- and the kit's own probe measures that stage 7 ok / 0 failed against this gate. Taking the kit's stage now would be a second stage for a configuration this gate already builds and tests; whether to also carry the kit's probe file in tools/kit-probes/ is parked with Harri. **`revision` and every `kit_sha256` are UNCHANGED by this commit**: nothing here came from the kit, and being behind the kit is not a failure -- the check that called it one was measuring whether the kit had moved. **2026-09-20, card t_9541aa62:** `tools/ci.sh` gained ONE line the kit does not have -- `unset GIT_INDEX_FILE` in the prologue -- because git exports its TEMPORARY index to the pre-commit hook for a pathspec commit (`git commit -- <path>`), the FetchContent update step of the `build` stage inherited it and ran `git status` inside build/_deps/jsom-src against Computo's index entries, and died on a blob that clone's object store does not have (`fatal: unable to read 691e2bdafaf312970644391de042d38c2c5972d8`, jsom-populate-gitupdate.cmake:186): so a pathspec commit failed its OWN pre-commit gate at `build`, reporting a dependency-update failure for a tree that builds fine. The two decisions this change had to settle were measured, not assumed: (1) the mechanism, by hand in the dependency clone (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<Computo>/.git/index git --git-dir=.git status --porcelain` -> rc 128, that fatal; the same command without it -> rc 0, clean), and (2) WHERE to unset it, by running the gate's own tree/format stages BOTH ways inside a real pathspec commit in a throwaway clone -- identical inputs, byte-identical outputs -- which is what makes the prologue the safe place rather than merely the cheap one. With the line in, a pathspec commit runs the fast tier to GATE PASSED on this checkout and in a fresh clone. `revision`, every `kit_sha256` and both per-fix lists are UNCHANGED: this is a repo-local fix, so it is a PENDING PORT BACK to the kit rather than a port from it -- tracked as card t_0a9a0018, and the COMPUTO ADAPTATIONS block in tools/ci.sh and the new INCIDENTS.md entry both say so. Only two `repo_sha256` values moved: tools/ci.sh and INCIDENTS.md. **2026-09-20, card t_c1c5ba6c:** the GIT_INDEX_FILE fix is no longer a port back -- the kit carries the line, so this copy takes it FROM the kit. `revision` moved to f9c33005d880df095d7a5ab300d1ec5349c59aea (f9c3300) because this files[] set now takes `probes/git-index-file.sh` from it, carried byte-identical as tools/kit-probes/git-index-file.sh. The jump from 951608c covers TWO kit commits, and three of the values below move with it for that reason rather than as new ports: the release stage (d531a110) touched templates/cpp/ci.sh, templates/cpp/.ci.env.example and templates/hooks/pre-push, and the GIT_INDEX_FILE fix (f9c3300) touched templates/cpp/ci.sh and INCIDENTS.md -- so `kit_sha256` is re-read here for tools/ci.sh, .ci.env.example, .githooks/pre-push and INCIDENTS.md, and every other entry's is unchanged by it. What moved in THIS repo is prose plus the probe: the COMPUTO ADAPTATIONS bullet and the prologue comment in tools/ci.sh stopped calling the line the one thing the kit does not have and now say the kit carries it as of f9c3300 with the probe holding every copy to it; the INCIDENTS.md entry's `Check added:` names that probe beside the line. DECISION, with the reason: the repo-specific prologue comment block was KEPT rather than replaced with the kit's shorter one -- it carries this repo's own measurement (the five cmake configure lines, the same 103-entry source set, byte-identical tree/format outputs both ways) that the kit's generic block does not, and the kit's block names `probes/git-index-file.sh`, a path that does not exist in this repo (here it is tools/kit-probes/git-index-file.sh), so taking it verbatim would install a dangling reference. The one-line fix itself is now the kit's, and the probe is what keeps the two in step. `adopted_fixes` gains the entry claiming this fix in the RECORD-ONLY commit that follows this one, because `adopted_in` must name a landed commit and a commit cannot name itself. Only two `repo_sha256` values moved: tools/ci.sh and INCIDENTS.md. **2026-10-06, hook-tier port:** adopted_fixes gains hook-tiers-agree and the revision moves to 919006e, the kit commit that probe is carried from verbatim, with every kit_sha256 re-read at that copy point. tools/ci.sh gained CI_FAST_STAGES/CI_FULL_STAGES and the `fast`/`full` arguments; CI_DEFAULT_STAGES IS the full tier now, which also fixed the drift recorded here earlier (the default list was two stages behind the hand-written pre-push list). Both hooks name a tier. The pre-push list's own comment, which asked a human to keep the two in step, went with the list. **2026-10-06, card t_075c0a6f (KitCI fleet batch 2 of 3):** the gate is no longer a bash script. tools/ci.sh and the probes under tools/kit-probes/ are DELETED; the gate is the tracked gate.toml (11 stages, tiers fast/full) run by kit-ci, plus scripts/gate-env.sh, scripts/gate.sh and one scripts/<stage>.sh per stage — all of them this repo's own files, which is why none appears in files[] below. files[] loses tools/ci.sh and every tools/kit-probes/*.sh entry: the artifacts are gone, so no hash can describe them. The kit fixes those probes guarded move from adopted_fixes to declined_fixes — not because the fixes were declined, but because the artifact they CHECK no longer exists (each probe is written against a single bash gate file; measured against scripts/gate.sh, see INCIDENTS.md for the verdicts). The contracts did not go: each one has a named home, listed in INCIDENTS.md entry by entry. .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push are RE-HASHED because this commit edits them: they now NAME a tier (--tier fast, and --tier full with CI_REQUIRE_CLEAN=1, the old --require-clean flag moved into the environment), and their branch for this repo's own tools/ci.sh is gone with that file. `revision` and every other entry are UNCHANGED: nothing here came from the kit, and being behind the kit is not a failure.

Per-repo incident log (401 lines here, 186 in the kit): it shares the kit's header rule block and then carries seven incidents of this repo's own — the wall-clock throughput threshold, the leak heuristic measured against the sanitizer's quarantine, the linter analysing a fetched dependency with one uncompiled source, and the 31-file format drift — while the kit's six entries (python src-layout, the tidy baseline recipe, the version stage, a repo's own defaults being ignored, sanitizer-hostile tests, the format example) are deliberately NOT copied: this file is history, so a sync must never overwrite it with the kit's. **2026-09-20, card t_45a28893:** the optimized-build entry's `Check added:` now names the `release` stage of tools/ci.sh, its measurements and the clone-based teeth proof, instead of pointing at a follow-up card. **2026-09-20, card t_4a81d75f:** a fifth incident of this repo's own — the docs pipeline had no local stage, and 41 result examples in the published README had drifted (29 of them still showing the pre-2026-02-10 array wrapper). The new `docs` stage covers the YAML half; the README half is stated as uncovered in the same entry. **2026-09-20, card t_a609b673:** a sixth incident of this repo's own — README.md's 99 prose result examples were graded by nothing (and an unbalanced code fence made the published page render a code block over the paragraph that followed it); the docs stage's step 2 now grades the examples, and the entry carries the reasoning for the extraction floor and for the two rejected alternatives. **2026-09-20, card t_9541aa62:** a seventh incident of this repo's own — a pathspec commit failed its own pre-commit gate at `build`, because git's TEMPORARY index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`, exported to the hook by `git commit -- <path>`) reached the FetchContent clone of JSOM and made `git status` there read Computo's index entries against an object store that lacks them. The entry carries the mechanism, the by-hand reproduction, the measurement that settled WHERE to unset it (the prologue, not per configure line), and the proof that a pathspec commit now passes on this checkout and in a fresh clone. **2026-09-20, card t_c1c5ba6c:** the GIT_INDEX_FILE entry's `Check added:` no longer describes the line as a pending port back to the kit: it names the kit's probe (carried here as tools/kit-probes/git-index-file.sh and run by the `kitprobes` stage) beside the line, and states the line as the kit's since f9c3300. The rest of the entry is unchanged -- it is this repo's own measurement.
